text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn yesterday denied that he was planning to reshuffle the cabinet. @

- Leaders of Hungary's major churches called on Premier Horn in his office Monday to launch the Love and Support '96 campaign to raise funds for the needy in conjunction with the upcoming Christmas and Hanukkah season.
- Parliament began a general debate yesterday on a bill to transform the state news agency MTI into a shareholders' company, with just one share, to be held by Parliament.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs yesterday welcomed Sunday's election of Emil Constantinescu as President of Romania, describing it as favourable for the development of bilateral relations. @
- Defence Ministry spokesman Lajos Erdelyi announced yesterday that Hungary is ready to continue to play a role in the Bosnian peace effort.
- The securities firm Co-Nexus Ertekhaz Rt. has voluntarily suspended activities amid allegations of misusing funds.
- The insurance company Generali Rt. expects to take in HUF 9 billion in revenue from premiums this year.
- Army engineers and mine deactivation experts yesterday removed about 100 kg of ammunition left over from World War II that was discovered Sunday in the village of Baracska.
NEPSZABADSAG @

- During yesterday's meeting of the Socialist and Free Democrat governing councils, Premier Horn rejected a Free Democrat proposal that coalition consensus be in place before the premier makes any foreign policy or governmental decision.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A report to be submitted to the cabinet later this week suggests that the price of electricity will go up by 23 percent and that of gas by 16-17 percent.
- The National Bank of Hungary has decreased active and passive repo rates by 0.25 percent as of today. @

- EBRD, the European Investment Bank and the EU's Phare programme have agreed to extend financing to the Hungarian state railway company MAV for the period 1997-2001, having concluded a review of its development plan.
- Morgan Stanley Capital International introduced a 'country index' for Hungary yesterday, which it will use to measure the performance of the Budapest Stock Exchange.
- Solo yachtsman Nandor Fa, who twice suffered setbacks in the Vendee Globe round-the-world boat race, has vowed to set sail again this week.
NEPSZAVA @
- Senior Socialist Party members admitted Monday that they discussed a possible cabinet shake-up at an informal meeting last week.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Istvan Nikolits, minister without portfolio in charge of the secret service, has denied a report carried by The Washington Times last week that US deputy secretary of state Toby Gati and Ivan Volgyes, professor and senior adviser to General Electric, had been in contact with Hungarian intelligence agents. @
- Hungarian enterprises and state organs invested about HUF 679 billion in the first nine months of the year, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The after-tax profit of the retail holding company Fotex came to HUF 374 million in the first nine months.
- Hypo-Bank Hungary Rt generated a pre-tax profit of HUF 392 million in January - September 1996.
